chapter: Lecture 5: Weathering of Rocks and Minerals — Types, Physical & Biological Agents
subject: agricultural_chemistry_and_soil_science

questions.stem: In evaluating rock permeability and lithological weathering rates, which statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Permeability is the most critical single lithological factor governing weathering rates.
options.B: Porous coarse-textured Sandstone weathers more rapidly than dense Basalt.
options.C: Polymineralic Basalt weathers more rapidly than massive crystalline Granite.
options.D: Coarse gravel deposits weather faster than fine volcanic ash because gravels have larger pores.
options.E: Fine volcanic ash weathers rapidly due to massive internal porosity and surface area.

questions.rationale: Permeability controls weathering; Sandstone > Basalt > Granite in decay rate; volcanic ash weathers faster than gravels. Statement D is false because water flows between rather than through gravels. (Key Takeaway: Lithological permeability and grain porosity govern weathering velocity.)

questions.stem: What quantitative thermal expansion relationships exist among rock-forming minerals and rock types? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Cubical expansion of Quartz is precisely twice (2.0x) that of Feldspars.
options.B: Linear expansion of Granite is half (0.5x) that of Sandstone.
options.C: Dark-colored ferromagnesian minerals absorb heat faster than light-colored minerals.
options.D: Feldspar cubical expansion is four times greater than quartz.
options.E: Differential mineral expansion produces internal microfractures along crystal boundaries.

questions.rationale: Quartz cubical expansion = 2x Feldspar; Granite linear = 0.5x Sandstone; dark rocks heat faster; thermal differential causes microfractures. Statement D is inverted. (Key Takeaway: Differential mineral expansion generates internal shear stresses along grain boundaries.)

questions.stem: Which quantitative stream velocity thresholds and sediment transport relationships are scientifically correct? (Select all that apply)

options.C: 1.2 m/s current transports heavy stones and pebbles.
options.D: 9.0 m/s current transports boulders weighing several tonnes.
options.E: Mechanical rock disintegration is vastly greater near a river's source than at its mouth.

questions.correct_answers: A, B, C, D, E (All options correct)
questions.rationale: All 4 fluvial velocity thresholds (15 cm/s, 30 cm/s, 1.2 m/s, 9.0 m/s) and the headwater disintegration gradient are verified physical principles. (Key Takeaway: Fluvial sediment carrying power scales precisely with current velocity.)

questions.stem: What physical and quantitative facts characterize Frost Wedging (Cryofracturing)? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Liquid water expands by precisely 9 percent (9%) upon freezing into ice.
options.B: Confined freezing water generates a lateral bursting pressure of 1465 Mg m⁻² (1465 tonnes/m²).
options.C: It is most effective in alpine and temperate regions with frequent diurnal freeze-thaw cycles.
options.D: Ice contraction upon freezing pulls rock joint walls together.
options.E: Frost wedging generates extensive scree and talus deposits at cliff bases.

questions.rationale: Water expands 9% upon freezing, exerting 1465 Mg m⁻² bursting pressure in alpine freeze-thaw zones, creating talus slopes. Ice expands rather than contracts. (Key Takeaway: Confined 9% ice expansion generates 1465 Mg m⁻² bursting pressure in freeze-thaw environments.)

questions.stem: Which statements accurately explain Eolian (Wind) Weathering and Sandblasting mechanics? (Select all that apply)

options.A: The sediment-carrying capacity of wind increases proportional to the 6th power of its velocity (v⁶ law).
options.B: Heavy abrasive quartz sand grains saltate primarily within the lowest 1 meter above the ground.
options.C: Differential vertical sandblasting sculpts Mushroom Rocks in arid desert landscapes.
options.D: Mushroom Rocks are prominent in the Aravalis and Thar Desert of Rajasthan.
options.E: Wind carrying capacity is strictly inversely proportional to wind speed.

questions.rationale: Wind carrying capacity follows the v⁶ law; saltating sand in the bottom 1m undercuts pedestals, forming mushroom rocks in the Aravalis/Thar. Statement E is false. (Key Takeaway: Wind carrying capacity follows the v^6 power law, sculpting desert mushroom rocks.)

questions.stem: How do living organisms drive chemical decomposition of minerals in Biological Weathering? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Plant roots secrete low-molecular-weight organic acids (citric, oxalic, malic).
options.B: Root-secreted organic chelating ligands bind and extract metal cations (Fe³⁺, Al³⁺, Ca²⁺) from silicate lattices.
options.C: Microbial respiration elevates soil pore CO₂ partial pressure, forming carbonic acid (H₂CO₃).
options.D: Subterranean termites and ants secrete biochemical formic acid (HCOOH).
options.E: Living plant roots absorb pure solid granite crystals directly into leaf tissue.

questions.rationale: Root acids, chelating ligands, microbial carbonic acid, and termite/ant formic acid drive chemical mineral decomposition. Plants cannot absorb solid rock crystals. (Key Takeaway: Biological chemical decomposition is driven by root exudates, microbial carbonic acid, and insect formic acid.)

questions.stem: Which activities illustrate the role of Fauna (animals and humans) in rock and mineral weathering? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Anthropogenic civil engineering (rock blasting, mining, quarrying for highways and dams)
options.B: Burrowing fauna fracturing rock horizons and aerating subsoils
options.C: Animal metabolic excreta reacting chemically with mineral surfaces
options.D: Termites constructing subterranean galleries and transporting deep mineral particles to topsoil
options.E: Fauna converting atmospheric nitrogen directly into liquid lava

questions.rationale: Human blasting/mining, animal burrowing, excreta reactions, and termite pedoturbation are verified faunal weathering mechanisms. Lava creation is volcanic. (Key Takeaway: Faunal weathering encompasses anthropogenic blasting, burrowing fracture, and termite pedoturbation.)

questions.stem: In the context of soil genesis, how does the weathering feedback loop operate? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Physical disintegration fragments rock, expanding total specific surface area.
options.B: Expanded surface area accelerates chemical hydrolysis and dissolution kinetics.
options.C: Released nutrient cations support biological colonization by pioneer plants and microbes.
options.D: Biological acid secretion further accelerates chemical and mechanical breakdown.
options.E: The feedback loop causes all soil to vanish into deep space.

questions.rationale: Physical fragmentation -> surface area expansion -> chemical hydrolysis -> nutrient release -> biological colonization -> further breakdown forms the self-reinforcing feedback loop. (Key Takeaway: Weathering processes form a self-reinforcing feedback cycle driving soil genesis.)

questions.stem: Which of the following are essential soil plant nutrients released through primary mineral weathering? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Potassium (K⁺) from orthoclase feldspar and micas
options.B: Calcium (Ca²⁺) and Magnesium (Mg²⁺) from plagioclase, pyroxenes, and amphiboles

questions.rationale: Weathering of primary silicates and apatite supplies essential plant nutrients (K, Ca, Mg, P). Plutonium is a synthetic transuranic element. (Key Takeaway: Primary mineral weathering is the original natural source of essential plant nutrients.)

questions.stem: What geomorphic and lithological outcomes result from Exfoliation on crystalline rock outcrops? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Formation of rounded, dome-shaped inselbergs and exfoliation domes
options.B: Concentric peeling of curved rock sheets parallel to the surface
options.C: Accumulation of curved spalled rock fragments at the base of slopes
options.D: Instantaneous transmutation of basalt into pure limestone

questions.rationale: Exfoliation produces rounded domes, curved spalling sheets, and basal talus debris in massive granite and basalt. Transmutation into limestone is impossible. (Key Takeaway: Exfoliation shapes rounded granite/basalt domes and spalls curved rock sheets.)
